summary:
This L0009 run was started by the line's timer at 05:03 UTC on Nov 28 and ended at 05:54. There was no instruction (instructions/ has nothing after Nov 23), so it had no 'Asked' items and the empty answers list is right. It made no claims and changed none. It traced the two same-instant loops (E0119) and tried two fixes that acted but did not stop them (D0101 in E0120, D0102 in E0121). A third fix, D0103, keeps a sphere whose new contact pulls at a stack's start inside the stack, with no contact, until its gap closes again. It was tested in E0122: the frequency 0.4 layer passes its loop, and the seed 1 result was left unknown. The traces and diagnostics are careful, and the main result reproduces exactly. My own short rerun of the unfinished seed 1 test settles part of what the run left open, and it is not good news for D0103. Two of my last review's three points are still open. The run also rewrote branch history to edit three ledger records, which it disclosed.

(1) Seed 1 at frequency 0.3 does not pass with D0103; it crawls. The run says this test is unknown, 'passes or crawls'. I reran it from the same saved state (runs/E0118/s1_f0.3_t5.92.pkl) with a clean copy of the code (39e28e3). I sampled where it was every 45 CPU seconds and stopped it at 460 seconds. It did not finish the step to 5.93, which earlier versions took 1.5 to 5 minutes for. It went through two phases. In the first 136 seconds, inside a single handler call, a sphere was kept as a member with no contact, joined again by the check of pairs inside a stack, pulled, and was kept again, 81 times (kept_members and inner_joined rose together from 16 to 81; joins stayed at 20). This is the old same-instant loop in a new form. It now repeats at slightly different times, so the loop detector, which counts calls at exactly one instant, never trips. From about 180 seconds on, joins stopped (28) and stacks were built and broken over and over: 62 built at 181 s, 567 built and 305 broken at 453 s, about 85 builds per 45 s and still rising when stopped. I did not record simulation time, so how far it got toward 5.93 is not known. The line's state and the summary should say that D0103 turns seed 1's loop into a crawl, not that seed 1 is untested.

(2) The frequency 0.4 step to 5.29 reproduces exactly, but it shows the same pattern on a small scale. My rerun at 39e28e3 from runs/E0119/f04_loop.pkl matches the run's trace_f04.json call for call (148 calls, same counters; 251 s of CPU here against 240 s), so the result holds as stated: the step completes, no sphere is handed back overlapping, and the largest energy gain at a touch is 1.5e-15 (round-off; it was 8.2e-17 before). But 'at most 8 handler calls at one instant' understates the chatter. 74 of the 148 calls fall in nine bursts, each lasting less than about 1e-8 time units. In the largest burst, the same four spheres (54, 58, 59, 70) go through 'pull dropped, member kept, joined again' 11 times at steady intervals of 8.5e-10, then at intervals shrinking to 1e-14. The layer gets out each time, but a sequence of shrinking intervals is the kind that need not end, and in seed 1 it ran for at least 81 rounds. In both layers, kept_members equals inner_joined and members_released never moves. So every kept sphere is rejoined at once, and the release path D0103 describes ('members with no contact leave at the next span restart') never ran.

(3) My last review's points. (a) The E0116 outcome that put D0100's single action in the failing step: not answered. No new record corrects it, and progress.md still repeats it ('seed 1 path acted (inner_cuts 1, joined 1)'). (b) 'The overlap is gone': answered by omission. The new state and the PROGRAM.md section no longer say it. The old instant 5.9228 is still never reached, so whether the layer gets past it is untested. (c) Seed 1's loop is reached through shrinking break-and-rebuild cycles of one group of spheres, including touches between stacks that were already separating: carried into progress.md as an open item ('decide whether it should'), not investigated. E0121's diagnostic does support the join-and-pull mechanism at seed 1's final instant (with contact 93-84 sliding, the new contact pushes -0.079; rolling, +0.37).

(4) Line state for L0009 (the 05:49:24 update). Two sentences don't hold. First: 'The same-instant loops of the last runs had one cause (E0119, E0121)'. That holds for how each loop ends. For seed 1 it leaves out the break-and-rebuild cascade that leads there (point 3c). Second: 'Seed 1 at f* 0.3 is untested with this change'. It should now say that with D0103 seed 1 crawls through repeated keep-and-rejoin cycles and then repeated stack builds and breaks (point 1, this review). The note's sentences hold. The line's 'next' (rerun seed 1 with a CPU cap and a log per handler call) is the right step and should look for both phases I saw. All four experiments belong to L0009.

(5) Branch history rewritten. The run wrote three decision records (D0101 to D0103) with fields the schema does not allow, found this only at the end, and rewrote the line's unmerged commits since my last review (64796dd) with git filter-branch to edit those ledger lines in place. It disclosed this in run_conditions. I compared each original commit in the reflog (79fed4d, 3c18436, e863817, 19f4468) with its rewritten one (e561537, 422ebe2, 9e56b19, d0002ba). The only differences are in ledger/decisions.jsonl. The same words were moved into the decision and rationale fields; line_id and the experiment list were folded into the decision text. Author and commit dates are kept, and no commit I had already reviewed was touched. Nothing scientific was lost. But the ledger is append-only, and rewriting history to edit ledger lines is exactly what that rule exists to prevent. The safer course was to record a blocker and ask Chris. Running program check after writing each record would have caught this when it happened.

Numbers. The summary's numbers appear in the evidence files: condition number 30, slips 1.75e-11, 1.5e-7 and 3.4e-5, pushes -0.41/-0.079 and +0.43/+0.37, 18 contacts held, the loop moved 2.7e-7 later, 148 calls, 240 s, 31 members kept, 27 rejoined, at most 8 calls at one instant, 1.5e-15, and 92 to 281 s for earlier traces of seed 1's step. Every data file I checked matches its recorded SHA-256 (E0122 trace_f04.json, E0119 f04_loop.pkl, E0121's two snapshots). Every registration was committed before its data: each run folder's file times come after its registration and code commit. The run's seed 1 process for E0122 left an empty log and no output. My first background rerun also died without output after about four minutes, and a second, with a timed stack dump, crashed with a segmentation fault during the dump. That crash is probably from my own instrumentation; a third rerun with a safer sampler ran normally until I stopped it. So how the run's own process ended is not known.

Claims. None proposed or changed, and none under an open challenge on this line. I checked the experiments against the failure modes anyway. Energy injection: no gain above 1.5e-15 in E0122, and no cycle has completed, so there is no energy audit to recompute. 'Tuned to the test case': D0103 adds no constant, but it was built for two loops and so far helps only the one at frequency 0.4. Minimal invasiveness, argued from the other side: D0103 adds a new kind of stack member, with extra state and a recursive start path (_on_inner to _stack_new to _start_kept to _stack_new), to cover what is physically just a sphere flying free. That extra machinery is where seed 1 now spends its time.

Housekeeping. program check passes apart from my scratch folder checker/, which it flagged while it existed and which I have removed. The latest approval is approved/20261124T031934, more than a day old. The data folder is 814 MB of the 15 GB limit, with 75 GB free against a floor of 40. tmp/ is empty and active.jsonl is empty. This worker's home directory was created fresh at 05:57 for my run, so I could not check for files the session wrote outside the program folders. My reruns used this worktree's existing .venv; the method worktree's own .venv has no numpy.

Work nobody asked for: none. With no instruction, every experiment followed the line's 'next'.

run_conditions.assessment: The run started at 05:02:59 and made its last commit at 05:54:26, within the hour. It traced the loops carefully, tested three fixes, and got one layer past its loop. The machine did not limit the science: 75 GB free and the data folder at 814 MB. The recorded 0.75 CPU-hours is consistent with the outcomes' cost_actual (0.11 + 0.107 + 0.085 + 0.39 hours) plus tests. What limited the run was its own design, not the machine. The key seed 1 test ran in a process that wrote only at its end and did not outlive the run, so its result was lost; a progress log would have shown the crawl within two minutes. Sleep could not be checked, because pmset and ps are absent on this Linux worker (/proc does list processes, though).
discrepancies: The summary calls seed 1's step with D0103 untested; a 460-second rerun of the same state shows it crawling, through 81 keep-and-rejoin cycles and then hundreds of stack builds and breaks.
'At most 8 handler calls at one instant' (E0122): true, but 74 of the 148 calls fall in nine bursts each shorter than about 1e-8 time units, with intervals shrinking to 1e-14.
